test_title: PYST 5: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 29 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Fill in the blank:
AQI values above ______ indicate unhealthy air quality for sensitive groups.
solution:
The correct answer is __**100**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Air Quality Index (AQI)** is a standardized system used to report daily air quality and its potential health effects. It focuses on health effects individuals might experience within a few hours or days after breathing polluted air.

• The **AQI** scale typically ranges from **0 to 500**. An **AQI value of 100** generally corresponds to the **National Ambient Air Quality Standard** for the pollutant, which is the level set by regulatory bodies like the **Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)** or the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** to protect public health.

• When **AQI** values are between **101 and 150**, the air quality is classified as **Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups**. This means that while the general public may not be immediately affected, people with **lung disease**, **asthma**, **children**, and **older adults** are at a greater risk from exposure to ozone or particle pollution. ***Hence, the statement that values above 100 indicate unhealthy air for sensitive groups is correct.***

• An **AQI** value of **50** or below represents **Good** air quality with little to no health risk. ***Hence, the option 50 is incorrect as it is within the safe range.***

• An **AQI** value of **75** falls within the **Moderate** or **Satisfactory** range (**51 to 100**), where air quality is acceptable but may pose a slight risk for a very small number of people who are unusually sensitive to air pollution. ***Hence, the option 75 is incorrect.***

• An **AQI** value of **25** is well within the **Good** category, indicating very clean air. ***Hence, the option 25 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• In **India**, the **National Air Quality Index (NAQI)** was launched by the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change** on **17 September 2014**. It was developed as part of the **Swachh Bharat Abhiyan** to provide a **One Color-One Number-One Description** for the common man to judge air quality.

• The **Indian AQI** system categorizes air quality into **six levels**: **Good (0-50)**, **Satisfactory (51-100)**, **Moderately Polluted (101-200)**, **Poor (201-300)**, **Very Poor (301-400)**, and **Severe (401-500)**.

• The **NAQI** monitors **eight major pollutants** to calculate the index: **Particulate Matter (PM10)**, **Particulate Matter (PM2.5)**, **Nitrogen Dioxide (NO2)**, **Sulphur Dioxide (SO2)**, **Carbon Monoxide (CO)**, **Ozone (O3)**, **Ammonia (NH3)**, and **Lead (Pb)**.

• The **sub-index** for each pollutant is calculated based on its **24-hour average** concentration (except for **CO** and **O3**, which use **8-hour** averages), and the overall **AQI** is determined by the highest sub-index among the pollutants.

• **Sensitive groups** include individuals with pre-existing **respiratory conditions** like **COPD** or **bronchitis**, **cardiovascular diseases**, **pregnant women**, and **infants** whose lungs are still developing.

**Important Points__**

• **PM2.5** (particles smaller than **2.5 micrometers**) is considered the most dangerous pollutant because its small size allows it to penetrate deep into the **lungs** and enter the **bloodstream**, causing long-term health issues.

• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** updated its **Global Air Quality Guidelines** in **2021**, significantly lowering the recommended limits for key pollutants, reflecting the increased evidence of health impacts even at lower concentrations.

• During **winter months** in **North India**, the **AQI** often enters the **Severe** category (above **400**) due to factors like **stubble burning**, **vehicular emissions**, and **meteorological conditions** such as **temperature inversion**.

• The **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)**, a statutory organization under the **Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974**, is responsible for maintaining the **National Air Quality Monitoring Programme (NAMP)** across **India**.
